test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 01 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has an error in its tense. Identify the error and select the correct sentence from the options.

If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allow you to go.

options.text: If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would allow you to go.
If you can apprise me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.

solution:
The correct answer is 'C'' i.e. "If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go." which corrects the tense error in the sentence..

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In conditional sentences that discuss hypothetical past events, the correct structure is "**If + past perfect, would have + past participle".**
 
• The original sentence incorrectly uses "**allow**" instead of the correct form "allowed".
 
• **Option 3** correctly uses both the past perfect ("had apprised") and the past participle ("would have allowed").
 
• Options 1, 2, and 4 do not follow the correct conditional structure or tense.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.*
